 SLL’s Korean drama "Something in the Rain" adapted for Indian market 
 Produced by Pocket Aces, the local adaptation airs on COLORS and streams on JioHotstar, marking SLL’s latest IP expansion into South Asia.

 "Something in the Rain"
 Share 
 SLL has expanded the global footprint of its IP with the official Indian adaptation of its romance drama "Something in the Rain." Titled "Shayad Yahi Hai Pyaar" (Maybe This Is Love), the remake is produced by Pocket Aces and currently airs on the linear channel COLORS while streaming on JioHotstar. 
 The Indian adaptation stars Aditi Dev Sharma, Daksh Puri, and Kunal Karan Kapoor and adapts the narrative to reflect contemporary Indian family dynamics and societal expectations around age-gap relationships. The original series, starring Son Ye-jin and Jung Hae-in, aired on JTBC in 2018 and achieved strong domestic ratings growth, climbing from a 3.8% premiere to a 7.1% finale share.
 "The adaptation of 'Something in the Rain' into 'Shayad Yahi Hai Pyaar' was an opportunity to bring a globally acclaimed love story to Indian audiences while preserving the emotional depth and authenticity that made the original so compelling," said Sameer Gogate, Business Head at COLORS - JioStar. "The encouraging response reaffirms our belief that powerful storytelling transcends geographies and languages when it is rooted in genuine human emotions." 
 Vinay Pillai, CEO at Pocket Aces, noted : "With the growing popularity of K-dramas in India, adapting 'Something in the Rain' presented an exciting opportunity to bring a much-loved Korean story to Indian audiences while preserving the emotional depth and essence of the original. We’re delighted to have partnered with SLL to bring this story to life." 
 "'Shayad Yahi Hai Pyaar' shows how a Korean story can be reshaped for local audiences without losing what made the original special," added Charles Park, Head of Content Business Division at SLL . "We look forward to working with more local partners to bring SLL’s stories to viewers around the world."
